values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem and RemoveCatalogItem (lines 65-82), and CreateAvailableStock (lines 99-117), modify persistent catalog/pricing and inventory data exposed through WCF OperationContracts. These security-relevant write paths call SaveChanges without any application audit/logging of the operation, affected record, caller, outcome or failure. Web.config lines 22-43 defines service behavior without serviceSecurityAudit or an application audit facility. Ordinary host access logs, if enabled externally, would not establish record-level change auditing. Finding is absence of an application audit trail, not proof of disabled infrastructure logging.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence: Assessed existing authored service/client source, configuration/transforms, application manifest and connection-string resolution. No hard-coded password, cryptographic key or authentication credential identified. Connection strings use LocalDB/named configuration or an environment-variable override; public assembly tokens are not secret keys. No explicit unsafe filesystem/resource ACL assignment found; missing endpoint authentication is not automatically classified as incorrect permission assignment. Confirmed absence of application auditing on reachable persistent-data mutation paths. Generated sources excluded; secret values are not included.
result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
